caption:
A brief that only has to satisfy the person reading it today isn't doing its job. It has to hold up when it's read again later — by an inquiry, an auditor, a court, a successor who wasn't in the room.

That's the standard we build to. Every output carries its confidence level and its basis: what was observed, what was inferred, what wasn't visible at all. We don't round an assessment up to a confirmation to make the brief feel more decisive. We don't round a gap down to zero to make the coverage feel more complete.

This isn't caution for its own sake. It's what lets a decision made on our output survive scrutiny after the fact — including scrutiny we don't control the timing of.

card.headline: Built to survive scrutiny, not just the moment
card.sub: Confidence is graded and basis is logged, because the record has to hold up after the fact — not just read well the day it's issued.

rationale: States the firm's accountability-first operating philosophy plainly, without boasting, and without repeating the grading/logging phrasing already used in prior PROOF-style posts.
